data.title: Stock index futures rise after weak payrolls report
data.description:
Stock index futures rose on Friday after July's nonfarm payrolls surprised to the downside, showing an unexpected contraction in employment.

Dow futures (INDU) +0.3%, S&P 500 futures (SPX) +0.5%, and Nasdaq futures (US100:IND) +0.8%.

U.S. nonfarm payrolls declined by 23K in July, missing the +88K consensus and erasing the 20K increase in June, according to data released by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics on Friday. What's more, June's growth was scaled back by more than half from the initial print of 57K. Unemployment slipped to 4.1% from 4.2% in June, lower than the 4.2% consensus.

The 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) was little changed at 4.25%, the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) was flat at 4.68%, and the 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) was unchanged at 5.22%.

data.title: Blend outlines $31.5M-$33.5M Q3 2026 revenue outlook while urging caution on Autopilot modeling
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Blend Labs (BLND) Q2 2026

Management view

  • “The second quarter was another disciplined, profitable quarter for Blend. Revenue came in near the high end of our guidance range and non-GAAP operating income came in above the high end,” said Nima Ghamsari (Co-Founder, Chairman, CEO & Head of Blend), while framing strategy around “two pillars… Autopilot… and Blend 3.0.”

  • On Autopilot commercialization and early performance, Ghamsari (CEO) said “Autopilot became commercially available on July 1,” with “cumulative loans processed… to more than 45,000 today,” and “more than 65 lenders activated Autopilot.” He added: “our customers are seeing a 10% to 15% improvement in pull-through rates and 2 to 4 days of cycle time improvement,” and “we estimate that Autopilot is automating 4.5 hours of loan fulfillment tasks on average per loan.”

  • On early go-to-market signals, Ghamsari (CEO) said “6 lenders have already signed contracts that include Autopilot,” and highlighted a customer example: “including Onity, which is one of the largest mortgage servicers in the nation.” He also described monetization direction: “customers signing flat-fee one-year contracts for full access,” and “over time, our intent remains to move the paid tiers to a per funded loan model.”

  • On internal productivity (Blend 3.0), Ghamsari (CEO) said engineering “3.6x our throughput… with roughly the same headcount just since January of this year,” adding “we expanded to our go-to-market organization” and “in our finance organization,” with a consistent operating model: “The agent takes the first draft. A person reviews and approves.”

  • Jason Ream (Head of Finance & Administration) reported: “total revenue of $33.8 million,” with “Mortgage Suite revenue… $19.2 million,” “Consumer Banking suite revenue… $12.2 million,” and “professional services revenue… $2.4 million.” He added profitability and cash metrics including “non-GAAP gross margin was 78.3%,” “non-GAAP operating income was $7 million,” “Free cash flow… $6.9 million,” and “$44.9 million in cash… and still with zero debt.”

  • Ream (Head of Finance & Administration) also emphasized capital return: “we repurchased 11 million shares at an average price of $1.65 per share,” and “Year-to-date, we have repurchased 22.2 million shares for $36.8 million,” leaving “approximately $13.2 million remaining” under the “$50 million” authorization.

Outlook

  • Ream (Head of Finance & Administration) guided Q3 total revenue to “between $31.5 million and $33.5 million,” and Q3 non-GAAP operating income to “between $3.5 million and $4.5 million,” citing a margin framework: “implying a non-GAAP operating margin at the midpoint of approximately 12%.”

  • Within Q3, Ream (Head of Finance & Administration) guided “Blend funded loan volume of approximately 200,000 to 210,000 loans,” “economic value per funded loan of approximately $80 to $81,” and Consumer Banking growth “between negative 5% and positive 1%.” He noted a temporary expense driver: “the third quarter expense includes our annual Blend Forum customer event… approximately $1.5 million sequential step-up in sales and marketing expense.”

  • For Q4 volumes, Ream (Head of Finance & Administration) said the company expects market size of “1.105 million to 1.165 million units,” and Blend funded loan volume of “approximately 180,000 to 190,000 loans,” while cautioning: “the macro backdrop remains highly fluid and sensitive to rates.”

  • Compared with the prior quarter’s call, Ream (Head of Finance & Administration) updated the macro reference point: “Fannie has lowered that outlook to about 17%,” versus the prior-quarter discussion that referenced roughly 19% full-year growth, and added a new business-risk datapoint: “we saw an uptick in churn notices this quarter.”

Financial results

  • Ream (Head of Finance & Administration) tied operating performance to guidance execution: “Revenue… near the high end… and non-GAAP operating income came in above the high end.” He also described Mortgage Suite unit economics: “Funded mortgage loans… approximately 233,000,” while “economic value per funded loan… $79,” and reiterated the seasonal math: “the step down from $83 in Q1 is primarily mathematical.”

  • On margins and Autopilot costs, Ream (Head of Finance & Administration) said “non-GAAP gross margin was 78.3%,” and added: “gross margin improvement is despite the model costs for Autopilot, which were relatively low but growing in Q2,” while “we expect those costs to remain fairly insignificant relative to our P&L for the near future.”

  • On customer retention dynamics affecting the model, Ream (Head of Finance & Administration) said: “we expect the revenue impact to be manageable in the low single digits of annual revenue,” as customers “plan to move to lower cost or free point solutions.”

Q&A

  • Aaron Kimson, Citizens JMP Securities: asked whether the prior view that agents could drive “10% to 15% incremental revenue growth in '27” still holds; Nima Ghamsari (CEO) responded “Yes, I don't want to give any additional further guidance there, but yes,” adding “those things take time,” while citing that “some of the biggest banks… push the rest of their organization to get this into place.”

  • Aaron Kimson, Citizens JMP Securities: asked when Blend 3.0 throughput converts to “revenue or operating leverage”; Ghamsari (CEO) said “it does take time,” and emphasized focus: “I focused our team internally on the medium term, which is 2027.”

  • Pallav Saini, Canaccord Genuity: asked whether Autopilot is available for Consumer Banking; Ghamsari (CEO) said “we do not have that live yet, but I'd say stay tuned,” and described product rollout timing as “over the course of a quarter or 2.”

  • Huan Chong (for Ryan Tomasello, KBW): asked about churn and whether it is “AI native point solutions”; Jason Ream (Head of Finance & Administration) said “we saw people going to existing low-cost providers,” and tied the driver to customer cost pressure: “they're looking for ways to save money.”

  • Dylan Becker, William Blair: asked about workflow “orchestrate the entire funnel”; Ghamsari (CEO) contrasted competitors’ “layer on something new” approach with Autopilot’s direction, stating the goal is moving “from that real time offer to clear to close,” and “we're going to keep working until the loans are ready to close at 2:00 a.m. in the morning.”

  • Dylan Becker, William Blair: asked why evPFL is expected to step up in Q3; Ream (Head of Finance & Administration) said “our volume expectations aren't that much different for Q2 and Q3,” and “it's mostly just the dynamics in the business.”

Sentiment analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly positive but probing, focusing on durability and timing of AI monetization and retention, including questions on whether “10% to 15% incremental revenue growth in '27” still holds, when AI productivity becomes “revenue or operating leverage,” and “the uptick on churn notices.”

  • Management tone was slightly positive in prepared remarks and more cautious on forecasting in Q&A, pairing confidence statements with timing caveats; Ghamsari (CEO) said “my confidence is very high” on customer leaning-in, while Ream (Head of Finance & Administration) reiterated: “we continue to encourage you to be cautious about incorporating Autopilot revenue into your models at this juncture.”

  • Versus the prior quarter, management messaging shifted from preview/beta and “move to paid tiers” to a post-launch footing (“commercially available on July 1”) while adding more explicit caution around churn notices and a more conservative macro stance.

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • Autopilot progressed from Q1 beta/preview (“use it for free… for all of Q2” and planned paid tiers “starting at the end of June”) to Q2 commercialization (“commercially available on July 1”) and initial contracting (“6 lenders have already signed contracts”).

  • Q2 introduced a new headwind not emphasized in Q1: “an uptick in churn notices,” with customers moving to “lower cost or free point solutions,” while both quarters reiterated macro sensitivity to rates.

  • Internal AI productivity claims intensified from Q1’s “more than 1.5x productivity” to Q2’s “3.6x” engineering throughput framing, with expanded rollout into go-to-market and finance workflows.

Risks and concerns

  • Ream (Head of Finance & Administration) warned of macro uncertainty and rate sensitivity, including: “we expect refinance volumes to remain muted in a higher for longer rate environment,” and “the macro backdrop remains highly fluid and sensitive to rates.”

  • Ream (Head of Finance & Administration) flagged churn risk: “we saw an uptick in churn notices this quarter,” and said customers are seeking “existing low-cost providers,” though he expects impact “manageable in the low single digits of annual revenue.”

  • Management emphasized modeling uncertainty for the new product: “be cautious about incorporating Autopilot revenue into your models at this juncture.”

Final takeaway

Management described Q2 as a profitable quarter with revenue near the high end of guidance and operating income above it, alongside active share repurchases and a cash balance with zero debt. The call centered on Autopilot’s post-July 1 commercialization, early operating metrics (pull-through and cycle-time improvements), and contract momentum, while also adding caution: macro-driven volume sensitivity, an uptick in churn notices, and explicit guidance to avoid baking Autopilot revenue into near-term models until more time and data accumulate.

data.title: HeartCore to sell 51% stake in Vietnam software JV for $184K
data.description:
• HeartCore (HTCR) announced on Friday that it agreed to sell its 51% stake in HeartCore Luvina Vietnam to its JV partner, Luvina Software Joint Stock Company, for JPY 29M (about $184K).
  • The sale will give Luvina full ownership of the Vietnam-based software development business.
  • HeartCore said the transaction is part of its strategy to streamline its business portfolio and focus on its Go IPO consulting and financial services businesses.
  • CEO Sumitaka Kanno said the deal will simplify the company's operations and allow it to focus resources on its long-term growth initiatives.
  • Following the news, the HeartCore stock dropped over 3% to ~$2.48 in the pre-market hours.

data.title: Intellia upgraded at Evercore ISI on nex-z hypothesis
data.description:
Shares of Intellia Therapeutics (NTLA) traded higher in the premarket on Friday after Evercore ISI upgraded the gene-editing biotech to Outperform from Inline, citing the company’s latest findings on nex-z, a rare-disease therapy it is developing with Regeneron (REGN).

The upgrade came after Intellia (NTLA) CEO John Leonard, during the company’s Q2 2026 earnings call on Thursday, detailed a hypothesis explaining a liver-related Grade 4 adverse event that prompted the FDA to impose a clinical hold on two late-stage trials for nex-z last year.

Since then, the FDA has lifted the clinical hold on both the MAGNITUDE and MAGNITUDE-2 trials, which are targeted at patients with transthyretin amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) and transthyretin amyloidosis with polyneuropathy (ATTR-PN), respectively.

The company “has finally shared a working hypothesis on the nex-z liver tox signal" that interrupted MAGNITUDE and MAGNITUDE-2 trials, Evercore analyst Jonathan Miller wrote as he upgraded the stock and raised its price target to $24 from $16.

The analyst added that “he is coming off the sidelines” as the hypothesis suggesting that “patients carrying a specific HLA allele known as C*05:01" appeared to be at risk of developing the immune-related safety signal was critical for his bullish view.

data.title: Most and least shorted utilities stocks with market caps up to $2B as of end-July
data.description:

data.title: Wendy's new CEO takes on turnaround effort, pulls guidance, cuts dividend in half
data.description:
Wendy’s (WEN) second-quarter results highlighted the ongoing challenges of maintaining traffic at its U.S. restaurants, while inflation and higher labor costs continued to pressure profitability. Although results were better than Wall Street feared, they also reflected a slowdown from a year ago.

Shares last traded with a loss of 5% in Friday’s premarket trading. 

Notably, there was a 7% decrease in U.S. same-restaurant sales and -2.3% for international sales, both worse than anticipated. And while total revenue improved modestly—beating estimates by $13M --the company’s earnings declined to $0.18 per share from a profit of $0.29 per share in the same quarter last year, although better than the previous quarter.

The results—amplified by higher costs and lower traffic—compressed the company’s gross margin as well as U.S. company-owned restaurant margin was down 240 basis points to a better-than-feared 13.8%.

"Today we are clearly not performing at our potential. I returned to Wendy's because I believe we can fix our issues, and I am excited to work with our team and our franchisees to drive a strong turnaround," said Bob Wright, President and CEO, who returned as Wendy’s chief executive towards the tail end of the second quarter.

The disappointing results and heightened efforts to restore growth, increase traffic, and “formulate a comprehensive turnaround plan” led the company to pull its full-year guidance and cut its dividend in half to create additional investment flexibility. Wendy’s (WEN) will now pay a quarterly dividend of $0.07 per share on September 15 to shareholders of record as of September 1.

data.title: Trump says he's not going to criticize Warsh over policy - report
data.description:
"I think he's great. I won't be criticizing him," President Donald Trump said, referring to Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh, in an interview published on Friday.

After Punchbowl News asked if Warsh, who has been on the job for ~10 weeks, should avoid raising interest rates before the midterms, the president said, "Well, it’s up to him a little bit, but not completely. He’s got a board that’s very political… It's not totally up to him. It's up to the board."

Last month, Trump repeated his desire to lower interest rates, insisting that the U.S. should have the lowest rates in the world. At the time, he also acknowledged that rate-setting isn't Warsh's decision alone. Warsh has one vote on the 12-voting-member Federal Open Market Committee.

Earlier this week, Bloomberg News reported that Trump has called Warsh repeatedly since he became Fed Chair in May, raising fears that the president may try to influence monetary policy. A person familiar with the conversations said the president hadn’t broached the topic of interest rates since Warsh was confirmed by the Senate, the report said.

Dear readers: We recognize that politics often intersects with the financial news of the day, so we invite you to click here to join the separate political discussion.

data.title: Applied Optoelectronics jumps on Q2 results, guidance; Needham still sees $1B+ revenue
data.description:
Applied Optoelectronics (AAOI) was in the spotlight after the fiber optic cable company reported second-quarter results and guidance. Investment firm Needham said the firm is still on track to generate $1B or more in revenue. 

Shares rose more than 10% in premarket trading, while peers such as Coherent (COHR) and Lumentum (LITE) also saw gains.

“F26 revenue guidance was maintained, indicating a steep 4Q ramp while GM targets were pushed out 1-2 Qs. 2Q revenue (+86% y/y) saw strong 200G/400G sales (+440% y/y) with Amazon contributing ~25% of total revs and growing shipments of 800G,” Needham analyst Ryan Koontz wrote in a note to clients. “1.6T is now poised to ramp in 4Q due to tight DSP supply against a $200MM hyperscale order. While execution is tracking 'close' to aggressive financial targets, soaring optical transceiver demand and share shifts away from Chinese vendors opens a clear path to achieve transformative multi-$B revenue growth.”

Koontz maintained his Buy rating on Applied Opto but lowered his price target to $190 from $220.

Looking ahead to the fiscal third quarter, Applied Optoelectronics said it expects adjusted earnings to be between $0.11 and $0.26 per share. Revenue is expected to be between $255M and $290M, with the midpoint of $272.5M, slightly below the $273M analyst estimate. Adjusted gross margins are forecast to be between 29% and 30.5%.

data.title: Arcturus targets Q4 2026 Phase III decision for ARCT-032 as it regains global KOSTAIVE rights
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Arcturus Therapeutics (ARCT) Q2 2026

Management View

  • CEO Joseph Payne said Q2 2026 featured “continued execution across our rare disease pipeline and important strategic developments for Arcturus' vaccine franchise,” highlighting a Q4 2026 decision point for CF and a Q3 2026 data update for OTC deficiency.

  • On cystic fibrosis, CEO Payne said the Phase II ARCT-032 study continued “on schedule with active screening and enrollment ongoing across sites in the United States, Israel, and Turkey,” and reiterated that “the decision to advance our CF program into Phase III is expected in the fourth quarter, or Q4 2026,” with Thermo Fisher support triggered if Arcturus proceeds.

  • On OTC deficiency, CEO Payne said Arcturus “completed enrollment in our ongoing Phase II study, and all enrolled subjects have completed study drug dosing,” and added, “We expect to communicate the Phase II clinical study data later this year in Q3 2026,” alongside an update on the regulatory path forward.

  • On vaccines, CEO Payne announced, “Today we announced the conclusion of our sa-mRNA collaboration with CSL Seqirus,” adding Arcturus is “pleased to regain global rights to our commercial COVID vaccine product, KOSTAIVE, and to our self-amplifying mRNA platform,” and said the settlement included “a one-time cash payment of $12 million” and release from liabilities “with an aggregate value of approximately $16 million.”

  • CFO Dennis Mulroy reported, “Cash and cash equivalents were $191.5 million as of June 30, 2026,” and said, “We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet and cash runway of over 2.5 years through year-end 2028.”

Outlook

  • Management framed near-term catalysts around program decisions rather than quantified revenue/EPS guidance; no explicit revenue or EPS guidance was provided in the prepared remarks.

  • CEO Payne set the CF timeline as a decision event: “our new guidance is focusing on the decision to proceed rather than a data share or completion of enrollment,” and said the “next meaningful event for this program is that decision, which is guided for Q4.”

  • For OTC, CEO Payne said the Q3 2026 update is intended to be “a fulsome update on the OTC program that includes not only the Phase II data, but the requested Type C data, and providing additional detail with respect to the regulatory path forward.”

  • For the regained vaccine portfolio, CEO Payne said Arcturus is “evaluating opportunities to maximize its future value, including further commercialization and partnering pathways,” with Japan operations “very active right now with Meiji” ahead of the fall season.

Financial Results

  • CFO Mulroy reported revenue of $3 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, and said the decline versus last year reflected “Lower revenue … under the CSL collaboration as Arcturus progressed towards termination of the agreement and regaining rights to KOSTAIVE.”

  • CFO Mulroy reported R&D expense of $17.5 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, attributing the decrease primarily to “reduced salaries, wages, benefits, and facilities costs,” while maintaining a “disciplined approach to capital allocation.”

  • CFO Mulroy reported G&A expense of $11 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, saying it was “relatively consistent” with a “slight quarter-to-quarter increase due to legal fees.”

Q&A

  • Lili Nsongo, Leerink Partners: asked what to expect in the upcoming OTC readout (U.S. vs. Europe) and whether success hinges on diet liberalization vs biomarkers; CEO Payne said the update will include “the U.S. and European dataset” and “supplementary data … requested by the FDA,” while CMO Alan Cohen said endpoints will reflect “the totality of the data,” including “safety and tolerability … biomarkers … most notably ammonia levels and glutamine … [and] quality of life and functional measures.”

  • Pete Stavropoulos, Cantor Fitzgerald: asked about CF enrollment cadence, interim looks, and extending dosing; CEO Payne said management has “a high level of confidence with respect to the cadence of enrollment rate now that Israel and Turkey are participating,” while CMO Cohen said timing should allow enough data “through a balance of Q4” for the Phase III decision.

  • Kuan-Hung Lin, Wells Fargo: asked what dataset supports the Q4 CF decision and whether the open-label design means real-time visibility, plus any safety signals; CEO Payne said Arcturus will consider FEV1, LCI, high-resolution CT, and quality-of-life measures, confirmed “we will have access to data on an ongoing basis,” and added ARCT-032 has been in “over 50 participants to date” with “a high level of confidence in our safety and tolerability.”

  • Joohwan Kim, Citigroup: asked how the Thermo Fisher deal came about and whether Thermo saw interim data; CEO Payne said there was “significant interest from multiple large manufacturers,” and confirmed, “they had access to all the data.”

  • Jake Batchelder, William Blair: asked about hyperammonemic crisis rates in OTC and the U.S. regulatory path for KOSTAIVE; CMO Cohen said the Phase II design is “not looking to capture patients that are unstable enough” for frequent events, while CEO Payne said Arcturus has received “very clear guidance as to what is needed for us to get this approved in the U.S.”

  • Whitney Ijem, Canaccord: asked what quantitative CF endpoints could justify Phase III and about Japan economics post-CSL; CEO Payne said thresholds will be established “by us in this process,” and said Japan was previously a “three ways” profit split that “will be split two ways,” with details under discussion with Meiji.

  • Jinnie Kim, BTIG: asked whether regaining global vaccine rights changes cost/R&D trajectory; CEO Payne emphasized monetization via “commercialization” and “partnership,” pointing to portfolio targets including “seasonal flu and pandemic flu … RSV, and EBV.”

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly positive and detail-seeking, pressing for clarity on decision criteria and regulatory steps, including questions on CF interim visibility and what endpoints could drive Phase III.

  • Management tone was slightly positive and milestone-focused, repeatedly anchoring to specific upcoming events (Q3 OTC data and Q4 CF proceed/no-proceed decision) and pointing to strategic value from regaining vaccine rights.

  • Versus Q1 2026, management discussion shifted from emphasizing early tolerability milestones in CF to emphasizing a formal Q4 2026 Phase III decision trigger tied to Thermo Fisher contributions, while analyst questions expanded to include the post-CSL vaccine strategy.

Quarter-over-quarter Comparison

  • Q2 introduced a major strategic change versus Q1: CEO Payne announced the CSL Seqirus collaboration concluded and Arcturus “regain[ed] global rights” to KOSTAIVE and the broader infectious disease portfolio, alongside a $12 million cash payment and release from approximately $16 million of liabilities.

  • In CF, Q1 emphasized being “well beyond one month of dosing” as a tolerability milestone; in Q2, CEO Payne emphasized that “the next meaningful event … is that decision” in Q4 2026, with communication centered on proceeding to Phase III rather than interim disclosure.

  • In OTC, Q1 highlighted FDA direction and exploratory data needs; Q2 advanced operationally to “completed enrollment” and “completed study drug dosing,” and management set expectations to share Phase II data and the regulatory plan in Q3 2026.

Risks and Concerns

  • Management emphasized that inhaled therapeutics face tolerability challenges, with CEO Payne saying, “Humans just don't like to inhale foreign substances,” and framed ARCT-032’s differentiators as a “biodegradable, non-accumulating” lipid nanoparticle, a purification process to control inflammatory impurities, and an optimized nebulizer.

  • Analysts repeatedly probed uncertainty around open-label interpretation, endpoint thresholds, and timing of disclosures; management’s mitigation was to rely on a multi-measure dataset (FEV1, LCI, CT, quality of life) and to wait for a “larger body of data” before detailed tolerability commentary.

Final Takeaway

Management positioned the quarter around two near-term rare-disease milestones—ARCT-810 Phase II data and a regulatory path update in Q3 2026, and a Q4 2026 decision on whether to advance ARCT-032 into Phase III—while also reframing Arcturus’ longer-term opportunity set by ending the CSL Seqirus collaboration, regaining global rights to KOSTAIVE and a broader infectious disease portfolio, and pursuing commercialization and partnering options for the validated sa-mRNA platform.
